name: Direct Counter 4-4-2

slots.why: Distributes quickly to the wingers or forwards to start the break.
Support full-back stays reasonably back, but supplies width when the counter is on.

Central defender. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the counter goes forward early and the pair is not asked to build. Only one centre-back may use Cover.

Cover centre-back sweeps behind his partner, which suits a deeper block. Defend is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the counter goes forward early and the pair is not asked to build. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Winger (Support) is a quick outlet who receives the ball wide and runs at the defence.
Defensive central midfielder breaks up play and shields the back four.
Box-to-box midfielder is the runner who supports the forwards on the break.
Winger (Support) on the right, doing the same job as on the left.
Deep-lying forward (or Complete Forward) holds up the ball so the others can arrive.
Advanced Forward runs in behind the defence. Poacher is the alternate.

description: A compact 4-4-2 that accepts periods without the ball and attacks space quickly after regaining possession.
whyGood: The DLF provides an outlet while the AF and wide runners attack the space left by an advanced opponent.
whyThisShape: A flat 4-4-2 that sits in a mid-to-low block and breaks quickly when it wins the ball, using its two wingers, a runner from midfield and two forwards. It is the simplest way to counter-attack: few players stay forward, so the rest can defend.
whenToUse: Against a stronger or possession-based team that will leave space behind its defence, when you have quick wingers and forwards.
whenNotToUse: Against a team that sits deep and does not leave space to run into, since the counter has nothing to attack.

instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Reach the forward outlets earlier without turning every possession into a long ball.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Move the ball before the opponent resets, using the receivers and runners supplied by the roles.
instructionRationale.Pass Into Space: Lead the mobile forwards and midfield runners into space rather than requiring every pass to arrive at their feet.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Lower Line of Engagement: Let the opposition advance before engaging, keeping space for the forward outlets after a regain.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

keyRequirements: Quick wide players who can attack space immediately after regains
A mobile strike pair with enough movement to make direct transitions dangerous
One midfielder able to hold position and one with the engine to join counters
A compact back four comfortable defending without the ball
Opponents willing to leave space behind or around their defensive shape
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
